Produces the folder desired_spec.md + current_plan.md + loop.toml + approvals.toml under dev/transformations/<name>/.
- transform: Run review groups of a dev/transformations/<name> step until the approval gate blocks: continue an open group or open new ones (subject to the gate), author units in parallel, integrate and verify them serially, escalate failures, and record everything in agent_log.md. Loops across groups until the gate blocks or work runs out. Transformation-agnostic — every rule comes from that step's own desired_spec.md and current_plan.md, never from this script. - Point it at any folder under dev/transformations/ via args:{transformation:"mcfm-translate"|"mcfm-cleanup"|"pepper-kokkos-port"|...}. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 1	# Fortran → C++: target output for one MCFM file
2	
3	This file defines the rewrite target and correctness bar for step 1. The workflow lives in
4	`current_plan.md`.
5	
6	Paths are written as `software/mcfm/src/...`.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Contract
11	
12	This step advances by *settling* source files one at a time: each file is rewritten, then
13	recorded in `agent_log.md` with a status `σ` once the oracle `V` confirms the invariants `I`
14	still hold. A file is ready when its callees are already available in C++.
15	
16	Objective `f`. Translate every source file to verified C++. Progress = fraction VERIFIED of
17	translatable files (`python3 dev/workflow.py status`).
18	
19	Invariants `I` (hold after every settled unit):
20	
21	- The restored build passes and matches to 1e-13.
22	- No called symbol is invented; each `.cpp` includes its own header; cross-unit calls go
23	  through headers, not translation-era forward declarations.
24	
25	Oracle `V`. `jobrunner submit tests/mcfm` + coverage probe (`python3 dev/workflow.py verify`).
26	
27	Status set `Σ`.
28	
29	| σ          | class | reversible | runner sets | evidence in log              |
30	|------------|-------|------------|-------------|------------------------------|
31	| VERIFIED   | good  | yes        | yes         | covered + worst Δrel ≤ 1e-13 |
32	| TRANSLATED | good  | yes        | yes         | build pass (not covered)     |
33	| FAILED     | bad   | —          | yes         | symptom                      |
34	
35	Risky `σ` = FAILED. Up to 3 completed groups may accumulate before approval. The sections
36	below elaborate this contract; on conflict the contract governs.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Output shape
41	
42	One Fortran file becomes one C++ translation unit set, and the folder's `CMakeLists.txt` swaps
43	its `.f`/`.f90` entry for the new files:
44	
45	- **`<base>.cpp`** — translated code plus `extern "C" <base>_wrapper(...)`; when a matching header exists, this file should include `<base>.hpp>`
46	- **`<base>.hpp`** — direct C++ declaration for the translated C++ entry points used outside the translation unit
47	- **`<base>_fi.F90`** — Fortran shim with the original entry name calling the wrapper
48	
49	A Fortran module instead becomes a `.hpp`, a `.cpp`, and a `_fi.f90` that mirrors variables via
50	`c_f_pointer`. Follow existing rewritten modules in `src/Mods`.
51	
52	## Rewrite rules
53	
54	Rewrite line by line. Do not add a `main`, extra declarations, or invented names.
55	
56	| Fortran | C++ |
57	|---|---|
58	| `subroutine`/`function` | free function + `<name>_wrapper` in `extern "C"`; declare the reusable C++ function in `<base>.hpp` when it is used outside its own `.cpp` |
59	| `use <mod>` | `#include <mod.hpp>` + `using namespace <mod>;` |
60	| `real(dp)` / `complex(dp)` | `double` / `std::complex<double>` |
61	| `dimension(nx,ny)` array | `FArray2D<double> a(nx, ny)` |
62	| `intent(in/inout)` scalar | pass by reference |
63	| statement function | C++ lambda |
64	| `x**n` | `pow(x, n)` |
65	| `return` | `return;` |
66	
67	### Never invent a called symbol
68	
69	Keep every call already present in the source.
70	
71	- If the callee is already rewritten, include its `.hpp` and call the C++ function.
72	- If the callee is still Fortran, declare the plain Fortran symbol in `extern "C"` and call it
73	  with pointer arguments.
74	- If a needed module dependency has no usable C binding yet, stop and rewrite that dependency
75	  first.
76	
77	The readiness map exists so a file is only rewritten when its callees are already available.
78	Use the Draft tool's hints and seed examples when needed.
79	
80	## Header / source structure
81	
82	Follow normal C++ structure for translated code.
83	
84	1. If a translated unit has a `<base>.hpp`, the matching `<base>.cpp` should include it as the normal declaration point for that unit's C++ interface.
85	2. Treat the generated header/source pair as the default structure for translated C++: declarations live in the header, definitions live in the `.cpp`, and the `.cpp` includes its own header.
86	3. If one translated `.cpp` calls a C++ function defined in another translated `.cpp`, include the callee's header rather than adding a local forward declaration.
87	4. Use local forward declarations only when there is intentionally no reusable header yet and introducing one would not make the interface clearer.
88	5. Put declarations for reusable cross-translation-unit C++ functions in headers before they are used from other `.cpp` files.
89	6. Keep `extern "C"` declarations only for true Fortran or C interoperability boundaries, not as a substitute for ordinary C++ headers.
90	
91	## Silent traps
92	
93	Check these explicitly:
94	
95	1. Dropped calls, especially near-duplicate paired calls.
96	2. Missing parentheses around denominators after translating chained `*` and `/`.
97	3. Wrong `FArray` sizes or bounds.
98	4. Accidental 0-based indexing for 1-based Fortran arrays.
99	5. Missing module or `Need.hpp` includes.
100	6. A translated `.cpp` failing to include its own matching header when one exists.
101	7. Calling a translated C++ sibling without including its header when one exists.
102	8. Keeping translation-era forward declarations even though a proper header interface exists.
103	9. **Silent segfault**: the test process crashes without printing output, leaving no `FAILED` marker but also no `passed` marker. A test is only acceptable if each individual test case is confirmed **passed** in the output — the absence of `FAILED` is not sufficient.
104	
105	If numbers still disagree after checking, mark the file `FAILED` with the symptom.
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Coverage map
110	
111	A file is only verified if a test actually runs it.
112	
113	One representative process per directory for coverage probing. `software/mcfm/Bin/bench` is the
114	exhaustive runner and covers many more variants per directory.
115	
116	| Process | Directory |
117	|---------|-----------|
118	| `u d~ ve e+` | W |
119	| `u d~ ve e+ g` | W1jet |
120	| `u d~ ve e+ g g` | W2jet / BDK / loop |
121	| `u u~ e- e+` | Z |
122	| `u u~ e- e+ g` | Z1jet / loop |
123	| `u u~ e- e+ g g` | Z2jet / W2jet / BDK / loop |
124	| `-Pmodel=heft g g h` | ggH |
125	| `g g h` | ggH |
126	| `g g g g g` | ThreeJets (any variant works) |
127	| `g g h g g` | gghgg_dep |
128	| — | Mods / Need / Inc / Procdep — infrastructure, mark `TRANSLATED` |
129	
130	This mapping is also built into `dev/tools/index/build_roadmap.py`.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## Correctness bar
135	
136	A passing MCFM test must match to **1e-13**. That alone is not enough: the test must also be
137	shown to exercise the rewritten file via `dev/tools/coverage/coverage_check.py`.
138	
139	Each test case must explicitly show **passed** in its output. Confirming the absence of `FAILED`
140	is not sufficient — a silent segfault produces no output at all and would pass that check
141	incorrectly. If any test case does not show a `passed` result, treat it as `FAILED`.
142	
143	The status set `Σ`, its classes, reversibility, and required evidence are defined once in the
144	`## Contract` above. Record results in `agent_log.md`, not here.
145

- IGNORE `README.md`. It is written for humans.
- IGNORE `evals`. It is written for humans.

1	# Fortran → C++ plan
2	
3	This file says how to run step 1. The rewrite rules and correctness bar are in
4	`desired_spec.md`.
5	
6	> This Plan is the policy: it selects and orders the work over the ready set (see *When to
7	> stop*). The correctness contract — objective `f`, invariants `I`, oracle `V`, and status set
8	> `Σ` — lives in `desired_spec.md`; on conflict the Spec governs.
9	>
10	> Authority: the AI may modify only `agent_log.md`; `current_plan.md` and `desired_spec.md` are
11	> human-owned.
12	
13	## Each round
14	
15	1. Refresh readiness (see Tools).
16	2. Continue the open group if one exists. Otherwise check the gate (see Approval gate) before
17	   opening a new group.
18	3. Rewrite ready files and wire them in (see Resolution; the rewrite rules are the Spec).
19	4. Build and verify each file (see Verify); record each result in `agent_log.md` (see Log file).
20	5. Stop per When to stop; otherwise keep going.
21	
22	## Log file
23	
24	Keep the changing worklist in `agent_log.md` in this folder. Create it if missing and
25	keep it current. Use it for ready files, review groups, and per-file status. Keep durable prose
26	notes in the session log at the end of this file.
27	
28	Record each finished file as:
29	
30	- `- [x] <file> — VERIFIED (worst Δrel <value>)`
31	- `- [x] <file> — TRANSLATED (<reason>)`
32	- `- [x] <file> — FAILED (<what went wrong>)`
33	
34	Use paths like `software/mcfm/src/...`.
35	
36	## Approval gate
37	
38	Review groups live under headings starting with `Group` in `agent_log.md`. Humans do not edit
39	`agent_log.md`. Human approvals live in `approvals.toml` in this folder and should normally be
40	recorded with:
41	
42	```
43	python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest-blocking
44	```
45	
46	or, to approve the oldest pending completed group,
47	
48	```
49	python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest
50	```
51	
52	or, for an explicit group,
53	
54	```
55	python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate "Group ..." --by <name>
56	```
57	
58	Use the gate only when deciding whether to start a new group:
59	
60	```
61	python3 dev/workflow.py gate mcfm-translate
62	```
63	
64	Interpret it this way:
65	
66	- If a group is still open, you may keep working inside that same group.
67	- A completed group containing `FAILED` requires approval before the next group starts.
68	- Otherwise, up to 3 completed groups may accumulate before approval is required.
69	- A gate failure blocks new-group creation, not builds, fixes, or verification inside the
70	  current open group.
71	- The gate checks only whether a group is approved; it does not interpret `approvals.toml`
72	  `review_note` text.
73	- After a group is approved, agents should read any matching approval record in
74	  `approvals.toml` before continuing work related to that group.
75	- Treat review notes as binding human guidance for that group unless a later human
76	  instruction supersedes them.
77	- If a review note changes scope or forbids an action, revise that same approved group
78	  rather than opening a replacement group just to apply the review note.
79	- A revision keeps the original approval logic unchanged: the group remains the same group,
80	  but the agent must update code and `agent_log.md` so the final recorded outcome matches the
81	  approved human guidance.
82	- If a review note conflicts with an already-logged result, treat the group as follow-up work
83	  in place: fix the affected files, update that group's entries, and add a session-log note
84	  describing the revision before starting unrelated new-group work.
85	
86	Stop for human review only when the gate blocks the next group.
87	
88	## Tools
89	
90	Run these from the project root. Prefer the unified workflow interface:
91	
92	- `python3 dev/workflow.py refresh`
93	  - refresh the readiness map and symbol index
94	- `python3 dev/workflow.py draft <file.f>`
95	  - make a rough draft and dependency hints
96	- `python3 dev/workflow.py verify <file.cpp> -- <process>`
97	  - decide VERIFIED vs TRANSLATED
98	- `python3 dev/workflow.py gate mcfm-translate`
99	  - enforce the human approval policy between completed groups
100	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest-blocking`
101	  - approve the exact group currently blocking the gate
102	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --latest`
103	  - approve the oldest pending completed group
104	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate --list-pending`
105	  - show pending completed groups waiting for approval
106	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approve mcfm-translate "Group ..." --by <name>`
107	  - record a human approval for a specific group in `approvals.toml`
108	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approvals mcfm-translate --group "Group ..."`
109	  - show the approval record, including any review note, for a specific group
110	- `python3 dev/workflow.py approvals mcfm-translate --latest-approved`
111	  - show the most recent approved group and its review note for revision follow-up
112	- `jobrunner submit tests/mcfm`
113	  - full MCFM build + test run; run this before verification if MCFM is not yet built
114	
115	The low-level scripts under `dev/tools/` remain available, but `dev/workflow.py` is the preferred interface.
116	
117	## Resolution: which files to do next
118	
119	1. Only rewrite **ready** files from `dev/tmp/assets/roadmap_metrics.tsv`:
120	   - `deps == 0`
121	   - `blind == 0`
122	   - no generated `.cpp` yet
123	2. Optional: limit one run to one top-level `src/` folder.
124	3. Group ready files for review:
125	   - same folder or test topic
126	   - about 5 files per group
127	   - headings must start with `Group`
128	4. If there is already an open group, keep filling and fixing that group before opening another.
129	5. Rewrite the group, wire it into the folder's `CMakeLists.txt`, build, and verify each file.
130	   - After converting a Fortran source, move the original `.f`/`.F` into `deprecated/` under the
131	     same directory.
132	   - Follow the Spec's Output shape and Header/source structure for the translated files.
133	6. After a group is completed, check the gate before opening the next one.
134	7. After any required approval, refresh the roadmap again before picking more work.
135	
136	The map exists so a file is only rewritten after its callees are already available in C++.
137	
138	## Shell notes
139	
140	CodeScribe bash is restricted. In practice:
141	
142	- use plain relative paths like `software/mcfm/src/...`
143	- no `cd`, pipes, redirects, or `$VARIABLES`
144	
145	## Verify
146	
147	Mark the statement that writes the file's main output with `// @coverage-probe`, then run:
148	
149	```
150	python3 dev/workflow.py verify <file.cpp> -- <process>
151	```
152	
153	Use the process mapped from the file's top-level folder in the Spec. If verification work is
154	needed and MCFM is not built yet, run `jobrunner submit tests/mcfm` first.
155	
156	Interpret results as:
157	
158	- `COVERED` → mark `VERIFIED` once the restored build still matches
159	- `NOT COVERED` → mark `TRANSLATED`
160	
161	If build or verification fails, keep fixing the current group unless the gate is blocking the
162	start of a later group.
163	
164	## When to stop
165	
166	The *ready set* is the set of ready, not-yet-settled files. Each settled file leaves the
167	ready set and the readiness graph is acyclic, so the pass terminates. Stop only when one of
168	these is true:
169	
170	- a completed group needs human approval before the next group can start
171	- the ready set is empty (no ready file to work on)
172	- a real blocker requires a person
173	
174	Otherwise continue editing, building, testing, and verifying.
175	
176	## Notes / session log
177	
178	- Header/source structure and the infrastructure-folder coverage mapping (mark `TRANSLATED`)
179	  follow the Spec.
180	- If coverage shows no change, retry after a caller is rewritten.
181	- If numbers disagree, mark `FAILED` with the symptom instead of guessing.
182	- Add a dated note per session: what you changed, what remains, and any human decision needed.
